18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CA 90703

Agenda Materials
The complete agenda for this meeting is available on-demand at www.cerritos.us and at the Office of the City Clerk, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, 1st floor, Cerritos, CA, during regular business hours (Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., weekend and observed holidays excepted). Any materials submitted to the legislative body after distribution of this agenda will be available for public inspection in the Office of the City Clerk during regular business hours. Requests for agenda materials or meeting participation assistance can also be made by email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by phone at (562) 916-1248 during regular business hours.
PUBLIC OBSERVATION AND PARTICIPATION
The public can observe the meeting via livestream on the City’s website at www.cerritos.us, on cable television at Cerritos TV3, or in person in the Council Chamber.
Public Comments
Members of the public may provide public comment for this meeting in person at the meeting or by using the following alternate methods:
Written correspondence (hard copy or email): Public comments can be submitted via email to city_clerk@cerritos.us or by hard copy to the Office the City Clerk no later than 3:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Please identify the agenda item number in the subject line of the email or hard copy document. All written correspondence received by the 3:00 p.m. deadline will be distributed to the legislative body prior to the meeting. During the meeting, your name and summary comments will be read into the record. The document will be retained with the public record of the meeting.
Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Accommodations
In compliance with the ADA, any person with a disability who requires accommodation in order to participate in a meeting should contact the Office of the City Clerk at (562) 916-1248 to request accommodation. The City will use its best efforts to provide reasonable accommodations related to the meeting.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD THURSDAY,
SEPTEMBER 14, 2023, 7:00 P.M., IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL,
18125 BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA. COUNCILMEMBER VO
PARTICIPATED VIA TELECONFERENCE FROM THE LOBBY AT THE LAKE TAHOE RESORT
HOTEL, 4130 LAKE TAHOE BOULEVARD, SOUTH LAKE TAHOE, CA 96150, AND THE
MEETING AGENDA WAS POSTED AT THAT LOCATION IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE
CALIFORNIA GOVERNMENT CODE.

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by Vida Barone, City Clerk/Treasurer.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Alexa, Maria, and Russell Lingad, award-winning U.S.
  Dragon Boat National Team participants in the 16th Annual Dragon Boat Federation World
  Championship.

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Lynda P. Johnson
  Council/Agency Member Chuong Vo (via teleconference)
  Council/Agency Member Frank Aurelio Yokoyama
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Naresh Solanki
  Mayor/Chair Bruce W. Barrows

REQUEST FOR REORDERING OF THE AGENDA

Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, requested City Council consensus, pursuant to the provisions of Section
8.09 of the City Council Protocol Manual, to reorder the agenda in order to consider Closed Session
Items 12A and 12B (described below) at this juncture of the meeting. He affirmed the City Council
should review the relevant information in Closed Session prior to consideration of the related Open
Session agenda item (Item 9C).

The City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider Closed Session Items 12A and
12B at this juncture of the meeting (public comments were opened prior to the City Council recess
to Closed Session, as detailed below).

12.  CLOSED SESSION

  12A.  PUBLIC EMPLOYMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: Position of City Manager

  12B.  PUBLIC EMPLOYEE APPOINTMENT
  Pursuant to California Government Code Section 54957(b) (COUNCIL)
  Title: City Manager

The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who elected to
provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.
 City of Cerritos  Thursday, September 14, 2023, 7:00 p.m.
City Council/Successor Agency Regular Meeting  Page 2 of 12

12.  CLOSED SESSION (continued)

The City Council recessed to Closed Session at this juncture of the meeting, pursuant to the
aforementioned City Council action, to consider Items 12A and 12B.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT (ITEMS 12A and 12B):

The City Council reconvened into Open Session. Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, reported the City Council
convened into Closed Session to discuss Items 12A and 12B, as listed on the Closed Session
agenda.

Item Nos. 12A and 12B:

The Council concluded its deliberations as part of the City Manager recruitment process.
Pursuant to Government Code sections 54953(c)(3) and 54957.1, the following report was made:

MOTION: It was moved by Solanki, and seconded by Johnson, to appoint Robert A. Lopez as the next
City Manager of the City of Cerritos and conclude deal points for an employment agreement,
summarized as follows:

  •  Commencing November 4, 2023, Robert A. Lopez will replace retiring City Manager, Art
  Gallucci;
  •  City Manager Robert A. Lopez’ annual salary will be $272,043, subject to any cost of living
  increases (COLA) as the City Council may authorize for the City’s Department Directors;
  •  City Manager Robert A. Lopez’ benefits package will be the same as those available to the
  City’s Department Directors, including vacation, administrative leave, and other benefits
  and will be carried forward upon commencement of office of City Manager;
  •  City Manager Robert A. Lopez’ pension packages as authorized under CalPERS and PARS
  will remain in place and will be carried forward upon commencement of office of City
  Manager; and
  •  Other common terms and conditions relating to public agency executive employment are to
  be included, as agreed upon by the City Council and Robert A. Lopez (COUNCIL).

The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:

AYES:  Johnson, Vo, Solanki, Barrows
NOES:  Yokoyama
ABSENT:  None
ABSTAIN:  None

(Information related to the reordering of the agenda and consideration of Closed Session Items
12A and 12B is also cross-referenced in Section 12 of these minutes).

ADDITIONAL REQUEST FOR REORDERING OF THE AGENDA

Bill Ihrke, City Attorney, requested City Council consensus, pursuant to the provisions of Section

this juncture of the meeting. The City Council, by consensus, reordered the agenda to consider
Item No. 9C prior to the remaining balance of the agenda.

(minutes continue on the next page)

9.  NEW AND OLD BUSINESS (pursuant to City Council consensus direction to reorder

  Manager and authorizing implementation actions relating to the appointment (COUNCIL).

  The Mayor opened the public comments period. Noting there were no individuals who
  elected to provide public comment, the Mayor declared the public comments period closed.

  MOTION: It was moved by Vo, and seconded by Solanki, to:

  1.  Announce that the City Council appointed Robert A. Lopez as the next City Manager;

  2.  Direct the City Attorney and Fred Wilson, of Ralph Andersen & Associates, to finalize
  an employment agreement for the next City Manager, subject to the following terms
  and conditions:

  a.  Commencing November 4, 2023, Robert A. Lopez will replace retiring City
  Manager, Art Gallucci;
  b.  City Manager Robert A. Lopez’ annual salary will be $272,043, subject to any cost
  of living increases (COLA) as the City Council may authorize for the City’s
  Department Directors;
  c.  City Manager Robert A. Lopez’ benefits package will be the same as those
  available to the City’s Department Directors, including vacation, administrative
  leave, and other benefits and will be carried forward upon commencement of
  office of City Manager;
  d.  City Manager Robert A. Lopez’ pension packages as authorized under CalPERS and
  PARS will remain in place and will be carried forward upon commencement of
  office of City Manager;
  e.  Other common terms and conditions relating to public agency executive
  employment are to be included, as agreed upon by the City Council and Robert A.
  Lopez; and

  3.  Direct Art Gallucci, current City Manager, to take appropriate actions for the transition
  of responsibilities and to oversee the implementation of other necessary and
  appropriate actions for the appointed next City Manager (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (4 – 1) as follows:
